original_question: Assume (C, G) satisfies condition (N) and G_2 is abelian. Is it possible for the exponent of G_2 to be greater than p?
target_in_paper: Question 6.10 in §6.1.2 ("Big p-group actions: Nakajima condition (N)") of the section "Automorphisms of curves and stable reduction": "Assume G_2 is abelian. Is it possible for the exponent of G_2 to be greater than p?"
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right local object (G_2), keeps the standing hypothesis that (C, G) satisfies condition (N), adds the same abelianity assumption on G_2 as in the paper, and asks exactly the same exponent question as the official formulation in Question 6.10.
missing_details: The ambient field k is implicit in the paper: k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0.
C should be specified as a nonsingular projective curve over k.
G should be specified as a p-subgroup of Aut_k(C).
To make the question stand-alone, condition (N) must be unpacked: g_C > 0 and |G|/g_C > 2p/(p - 1) (Definition 6.2).
The surrounding discussion is in the g_C >= 2 regime of Question 6.4 and Proposition 6.3; this is the context in which G_2 is then defined via ramification.
G_2 is not an arbitrary subgroup: it is the second ramification group in lower numbering at the unique ramification point of the cover C -> C/G furnished by Proposition 6.3.
The meaning of p in the phrase "exponent greater than p" should be made explicit: it is the characteristic of k.
If one wants the paper-faithful equivalent reformulation, Theorem 6.7 shows that under (N), G_2 = G' = G'G^p, so the question can equivalently be asked about the commutator subgroup.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, let C/k be a nonsingular projective curve of genus g_C >= 2, and let G be a p-subgroup of Aut_k(C) such that (C, G) satisfies Nakajima’s condition (N), i.e. g_C > 0 and |G|/g_C > 2p/(p - 1). Let infinity be the unique ramification point of the cover C -> C/G given by Proposition 6.3, and let G_2 be the second ramification group of G at infinity in lower numbering. Assuming G_2 is abelian, can G_2 have exponent strictly greater than p?
equivalent_formulation: By Theorem 6.7, under condition (N) one has G_2 = G' = G'G^p. Hence an equivalent paper-explicit formulation is: if (C, G) satisfies (N) and the commutator subgroup G' is abelian, can G' have exponent strictly greater than p?
justification: The draft is targeting Question 6.10, not the neighboring Questions 6.6 or 6.11. The official question in the paper is exactly the same exponent question, with the standing convention from the surrounding paragraph that one always assumes (C, G) satisfies condition (N). To make that question fully stand-alone, one must import Definition 6.2 (what condition (N) means), the genus/ramification context from Question 6.4 and Proposition 6.3 (which identifies the unique ramification point and thereby the meaning of G_2), and the characteristic-p setting. Theorem 6.7 is the nearby exact reformulation explicitly proved in the paper and is therefore the only alternate formulation that should be offered.
